articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got socially engineered harder than a freshman CS student, letting attackers seize Obama's Instagram and Space Force accounts with pro-Iranian messages. When your chatbot falls for the oldest tricks in the book, maybe it's time to question that whole 'AI revolution' thing.

articles.title: VICTORY: Meta Strips Facial Recognition Code From Smart Glasses App After Public Outcry
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dumped AWS GovCloud keys and internal secrets on public GitHub like it's their personal blog. The agency tasked with protecting America's cyber infrastructure just doxxed itself spectacularly.

articles.title: Cheers to the Winners of EFF’s 18th Annual Cyberlaw Trivia Night!
articles.summary: Meta quietly shoved facial recognition into millions of phones via their smart glasses app, then backpedaled faster than a politician during election season after WIRED exposed their creepy surveillance overreach. Public outcry still works, apparently.

articles.title: Iran Signed a Ceasefire — Its Hackers Didn't
articles.summary: Check Point VPN got owned by a critical zero-day that's been getting exploited since May, with Qilin ransomware crew taking the victory lap. Another day, another enterprise VPN falling face-first into the vulnerability hall of fame.

articles.title: Chrome's zero-day Whac-A-Mole continues with fifth exploited bug of the year
articles.summary: UK government wants to scan everyone's devices for nudes 'for the children,' while Signal correctly points out this surveillance infrastructure will inevitably be repurposed for full-spectrum censorship. Privacy dies one 'reasonable' exception at a time.

articles.title: France probes compromise of gov messaging platform after account hijack
articles.summary: Chrome's fifth zero-day of the year got patched after active exploitation, netting the researcher a sweet $55K bounty. Google's playing vulnerability whack-a-mole at industrial scale.

articles.title: The Hidden Security Risk in Modern Networks: The Work Between Tools
articles.summary: Chrome's V8 engine got pwned via CVE-2026-11645, an out-of-bounds memory access bug being actively exploited in the wild. Another reminder that JavaScript engines are basically nuclear reactors made of C++ and wishful thinking.

articles.title: Reducing security operations complexity with Wazuh Cloud
articles.summary: FROST attack lets malicious websites track your browsing and app usage by timing your SSD operations through pure JavaScript. Your storage device's performance characteristics just became a privacy nightmare with no permissions required.

articles.title: CBSE OSM row: Pradhan 'incompetent', continuation in office insult to lakhs of students: Cong
articles.summary: Meta confirmed thousands of Instagram accounts got hijacked by tricking their AI chatbot into password resets, affecting accounts without 2FA. The age of social engineering chatbots has officially begun.

articles.title: CBSE retains COEMPT for answer-sheet scanning, shifts data to its own servers
articles.summary: Former IBM cybersecurity VP turned whistleblower, accusing Big Blue of covering up years of Chinese state hacking like it's 2023 corporate standard operating procedure. When your own security chief calls you out, maybe it's time for some soul-searching.
